name: Rhode Island
agency: Rhode Island Division of Motor Vehicles (RI DMV)
permitAge: 16 (limited instruction permit, ages 16 to 18), after a 33-hour CCRI driver education course and a computerized test (manual p.10)

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, certified by parent or guardian (manual p.12; RIGL 31-10-6)
teen.nightLimit: Limited provisional license: no driving alone 1 a.m. to 5 a.m.; exceptions: to or from work, volunteer fire/rescue/EMS activity (manual p.14), and since 2017 4-5 a.m. between home and a school-sponsored athletic activity with no school transport (RIGL 31-10-6)
teen.passengerLimit: First 12 months of limited provisional license: no more than one passenger under 21; immediate family/household members exempt (manual p.14; RIGL 31-10-6)
teen.phone: Under 18: no cell phone use at all, including hands-free, except emergencies (manual p.35; RIGL 31-22-11.9). All drivers: texting banned (manual p.36); hand-held use banned, hands-free allowed (RIGL 31-22-30, current text, newer than the manual).

notes: Handbook read: Rhode Island Driver's Manual rev. 08/2015 (PDF dated 2019-07-19; same file also at .../manuals/Driver_Manual_FINAL.pdf). Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers.

A newer manual appears at https://dmv.ri.gov/media/966/download?language=en, but dmv.ri.gov returns a Cloudflare bot challenge (HTTP 403) to curl and fetch tools; not read. A search snippet of it reports 40 multiple-choice questions; pass mark not found. Exam size and pass mark left null.

The 2015 manual says only that the test is available in other languages on request (p.10). Languages English, Spanish and Portuguese (computerized; printed exams in other languages by advance request) come from the DMV knowledge-exams page as reported by search snippets; the page itself could not be opened (403).

Permit test: through the CCRI driver education course, otherwise at the DMV main office in Cranston (manual p.10). Road test instructions are in English only, with a Spanish/Portuguese vocabulary list (manual p.12).
Permit supervisor: licensed at least 5 years and 21 or older, seated beside the learner (manual p.11).

Move over law is not in the manual. RIGL 31-14-3 (amended 2023): change to a lane away from, or slow down for, stopped emergency vehicles, tow and transporter trucks, highway maintenance equipment, roadside assistance vehicles and any vehicle stopped on the shoulder or breakdown lane.
School bus (manual p.51; RIGL 31-20-13): stop from either direction; no stop for a bus on the other side of a divided highway or in a loading zone. The manual does not mention center turn lanes.
The 2015 manual predates the 2017 night-limit exception and the later hand-held phone ban; current statutes used for those.
